en.title: Parcel Management System
en.text: A GIS-centric Real Estate Management System for the Lebanese Maronite Order (OLM), modernizing management of 20,000+ land parcels and buildings across Lebanon. Recipient of a Special Achievement in GIS (SAG) Award.
en.textFull:
Recipient of a Special Achievement in GIS (SAG) Award. The Real Estate Management System for the Lebanese Maronite Order (OLM) is a GIS-centric solution designed to modernize the management of OLM's 20,000+ land parcels and buildings across Lebanon.

Key goals include:

  • Centralized Asset Management: Replace fragmented records with a unified geodatabase tracking parcels, buildings, legal documents, and ownership history.
  • High-Precision Surveying: Standardize parcel boundaries using GNSS and drone-captured imagery, resolving inconsistencies in Lebanon's cadastral data.
  • Encroachment Prevention: Monitor illegal occupation via updated spatial records and legal workflows.
  • Legal Dispute Resolution: Automate tracking of parcel disputes, government appropriations, and zoning restrictions.
  • Future Scalability: Serve as a proof of concept for OLM's planned ArcGIS Enterprise deployment, enabling advanced analytics, dashboards, and web applications.
en.myContribution: Led the project end-to-end — architected the geodatabase schema for 20,000+ parcels, defined the field data collection workflow, and directed development of the custom ArcGIS Pro Add-in used for parcel editing and validation.

en.title: GeoLeb
en.text: High-precision coordinate transformation tools focused on Lebanon — open-source, cross-platform, and available as a Python library.
en.textFull:
GeoLeb provides high-precision coordinate transformation tools focused on Lebanon. Open-source and cross-platform, GeoLeb supports native and web applications as well as a Python library.

High precision. Lebanese coordinate systems. Open source. Cross platform. Fast & reliable.

en.title: Wild Fire Prediction
en.text: A machine learning and remote sensing model predicting wildfire occurrence in Lebanon using Sentinel-2 and MODIS satellite imagery.
en.textFull:
Develops a predictive model for wildfire occurrence in Lebanon by integrating machine learning (ML) and remote sensing techniques. In recent years, Lebanon has witnessed a rise in wildfire events that threaten forested areas, biodiversity, and human settlements. By leveraging modern geospatial technologies and data science methods, this study contributes to disaster risk reduction and improved environmental management.

Research objectives:

  1. Detect and map historical wildfire events in Lebanon using Sentinel-2 and MODIS satellite imagery.
  2. Extract and integrate environmental and topographic variables (elevation, slope, land cover, weather data, proximity to roads and settlements, etc.) for both fire-prone and fire-safe areas.
  3. Train and evaluate various machine learning algorithms for wildfire prediction.
  4. Compare the predictive performance of traditional ML and DL models.
  5. Develop an interactive platform to visualize data, perform wildfire predictions, and provide early warning capabilities.
en.myContribution: Directed the research and technical execution — defined the modeling workflow from satellite data extraction through algorithm evaluation, and led development of the prediction scripts and analysis pipeline.

en.title: Road Quality Assessment Using Sensors and Deep Learning
en.text: A multimodal deep learning framework combining low-cost sensors and computer vision to monitor road quality across Lebanon, integrated into ArcGIS Online for field validation.
en.textFull:
Lebanon's road network continues to suffer from aging infrastructure, heavy traffic, and limited maintenance resources, making systematic and reliable road-quality assessment increasingly difficult. Traditional inspection methods remain time-consuming, expensive, and difficult to scale. This thesis presents a complete multimodal framework that integrates low-cost sensing, machine learning, deep learning, and GIS technologies to deliver a scalable, data-driven solution for road condition monitoring in Lebanon.

Because no single data source can capture all road anomalies reliably, the system combines sensor-based vibration analysis and video-based deep-learning detection, as each modality compensates for the other's weaknesses and captures different types of defects. A custom Raspberry Pi–based sensing device was developed to capture synchronized accelerometer, gyroscope, gravity, and GPS data, alongside continuous front-facing video.

The vibration signals were aggregated into 1-second windows and modeled using several machine-learning algorithms (Random Forest, XGBoost, Neural Network, Logistic Regression, AdaBoost, CatBoost, and Decision Tree), each tuned through Optuna. Individual classifiers achieved test accuracies between 0.65 and 0.72. To maximize stability and reduce model-specific bias, the best-performing models were combined into a soft Voting Ensemble, achieving the highest test accuracy of 0.73, outperforming all standalone classifiers.

Visual road-defect detection was performed using two deep-learning architectures. YOLOv8 achieved an overall mAP@0.5 of 0.379 (best class: Manhole, 0.796), enabling fast online detection. To support high-precision GIS-based mapping, a second model (Faster R-CNN via ArcGIS.Learn) was trained for detailed offline analysis, achieving a final mAP@[0.5:0.95] = 0.6012, with per-class AP scores of 0.5255 (Crack), 0.5386 (Bump), 0.3624 (Irregularities), 0.5321 (Manhole), and 0.8889 (Structured Surface).

A custom correlation algorithm was developed to merge sensor-based predictions with video detections, accounting for the natural time lag between visual observation and physical vibration. The correlated outputs were integrated into ArcGIS Online, forming a complete operational environment where dashboards, Experience Builder apps, and ArcGIS Field Maps support field validation, task assignment, and maintenance tracking.

Keywords: Road quality assessment, Sensing Device, Machine learning, Deep learning, Faster R-CNN, YOLO, Ensemble Voting, Accelerometer, Gyroscope, Raspberry Pi, ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, Spatial correlation, Infrastructure management, Lebanon.
en.myContribution: Owned the project from concept to deployment — designed the multimodal sensing-and-vision workflow, and led development across the ML pipeline, deep learning models, and ArcGIS Online integration.
